methodology: Decode steps of forward_paged_batch on CUDA bf16, block size 16. Each sequence is prefilled once to its target length; every measured step then rewinds seq_len so the next step sees the same context and overwrites the same KV slot. The step matches the body of generate_continuous_paged: one new token per sequence, argmax, then a per-sequence .to(cpu) and .item(). A second finish path reads the whole argmax row with one .tolist(), so the extra syncs are visible. Step time is CUDA events around the forward plus the host time through the token read, after a sync so the card is idle at the start of the sample. Five warmup steps, then twenty timed steps; the reported step time is the median. A separate pass of four steps puts two CUDA events around each named call. That span includes the GPU waiting for Python, so it is not kernel time; the profiler attributes kernel time to the same names. page_gather is inside gather_padded; the pad cost is the difference, and it is not added on top. weight_gemm is a matmul whose inputs are both rank <= 3 (the projections, the MLP, the lm_head). attn_gemm is a rank-4 matmul (scores and the attention output). The profiler runs two further steps. Kernel time is summed from the trace. A kernel is charged to the innermost GPU annotation that covers its timestamps, so page_gather is not also added into gather_padded. Gaps are the idle time between kernels on a stream. The profiler's own overhead widens those gaps; the uninstrumented CUDA-event span is the step time, and idle_inside_span_ms subtracts the profiled kernel-busy time from that span. Host is WSL2. Clocks are not locked. fp32 1.7B does not fit beside a CUDA context on this 8 GB card, so the profile is bf16.
